question: If 2frac{{{{cos }²}x - {{sec }²}x}}{{{{tan }²}x}} = a + b cos 2 x, then a, b = ?
solution:
**Given:**

2frac{{{{cos }²}x - {{sec }²}x}}{{{{tan }²}x}} = a+bcos2x

**Formula Used:**

cos2x=2cos²x-1 or cos²x=(cos2x+1)/(2)

a²-b²=(a+b)(a-b)

**Calculation:**

Simplifying L.H.S:

⇒2frac{{{{cos }²}x - (1)/(cos²x)}}{{{(sin²x)/(cos²x)}}} 

⇒2(frac{cos⁴x-1)/(cos²x)}{(sin^x)/(cos²x)}

⇒2((cos²x)²-1²)/(sin²x)

Applying property a²-b²=(a+b)(a-b) [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] 

⇒2((cos²x+1)(cos²x-1))/(sin²x)

⇒2((cos²x+1)(-sin²x))/(sin²x)

⇒-2(cos²x+1)

Applying formula of cos2x

⇒-2((cos2x+1)/(2)+1)

⇒-2((cos2x+3)/(2))

⇒-3-cos2x

Now, comparing the L.H.S with R.H.S we get:

a=-3 and b=-1

 **∴ The value of a, b is -3, -1.**
